title: Choose the visual world
question: Three directions for the app, each shown on the Pipeline kanban. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll. (Two more competitive alternates, a warm consumer-app surface and yellow airport wayfinding, wait in the re-roll pool to keep this to your three.)

options.label: Pipe Marker
options.thesis: The pipeline drawn as an actual pipe: each stage is a colour-banded marker with a flow arrow, and deals move downstream.
options.viewport: Enamel-green side rail; across the board, one continuous pipe whose marker bands are the column headers (count and annual CAD on each, arrow tips into the next stage); dense deal cards below with unit-code tags and an age bar.
options.risk: Band colours could read as safety signage if they spread past the headers and status chips.

raised.raise: Status is never colour alone: each band also carries a pattern (solid, hatched, striped), so colour-blind estimators read stages as fast as anyone.
Time is length: each card's age bar is exact days in stage on one fixed 30-day scale, so stale deals stand out without a number.
Density courage: cards pack unit-code tags (RTU ×6 · MUA ×1) edge to edge, so an estimator scans a whole site's equipment at a glance.

options.label: Equipment Schedule
options.lineage: Mechanical drawing sheets (M-series) and their equipment schedules
options.thesis: The app reads like the M-sheet estimators take off from: tag bubbles, schedule tables, grid references and redline revisions.
options.viewport: Drawing-blue rail with a title-block footer; the kanban is framed by sheet grid letters A–E; cards carry hexagon equipment tags, and a changes-requested deal wears a redline revision cloud with its version delta.
options.risk: The most familiar of the three: blueprint styling is where most runs for trade software land, and it can tip into costume if the grid ticks multiply.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: Airport gate boards and segmented boarding passes
options.thesis: Every deal is a departure: ranked by its next deadline, and a change lights amber and stays lit until someone notices it.
options.viewport: A black Next-up board strip ranks the next actions by time; below it, the kanban cards are segmented passes (customer, visits/yr, annual value, days), and changed cards hold an amber edge until acknowledged.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: deals rank by next deadline, and the hold-until-noticed state is exactly 'status is never in doubt'. Wins on product clarity, loses on audience identification because it isn't the trade's world.
options.risk: The black board can dominate if it grows past one strip; it must stay a summary, not the page.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: State carried by line height, dash and doubling on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: One off-centre rail with every stage a tick.
options.case: Loses both axes: contractors don't recognise it, and hairline state is too faint for daily pipeline triage.
options.kept: State by form, not hue: the Pipe Marker bands gained patterns.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Shape is direction, shading is level, length is exact duration.
options.viewport: A vertical centre staff read upward.
options.case: Loses both axes: a foreign notation for a trade audience, and a vertical time axis fights the left-to-right pipeline.
options.kept: Length is exact duration: age bars on a fixed 30-day scale.

options.label: Convention Catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of coded cells packed into a numbered grid.
options.viewport: Packed thumbnail grid keyed to a hall map.
options.case: Loses both axes: no thumbnails exist to pack, and the grid hides status.
options.kept: Density courage: unit-code tags packed edge to edge.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, familiar SaaS kanban like Linear or Trello, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: White sidebar, grey board, white cards with coloured status dots.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other tool by design.
